  bg-backup - pull request template

  Keep the sections that apply and delete the rest. An honest three-line PR
  beats a fully-ticked template nobody believes.

  Remember what this code is: Bash that runs as root, on a timer, unattended,
  and that is allowed to delete backup history. The checklists below are the
  mistakes that have actually cost people data - not bureaucracy.
-->

## What and why

<!-- What changes, and which problem it solves. Link the issue: Closes #123 -->

## Type of change

- [ ] `feat` - new capability
- [ ] `fix` - bug fix
- [ ] `refactor` - no behaviour change
- [ ] `docs` - documentation only
- [ ] `test` - tests only
- [ ] `ci` / `build` / `chore`
- [ ] **Breaking** (`type!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, and a migration note below)

## Blast radius

<!-- Answer these three; they decide how carefully this gets reviewed. -->

- Runs as root? <!-- yes / no -->
- Can it delete or overwrite anything in a repository (`forget`, `prune`, `restore --target`, `unlock`)? <!-- yes / no -->
- Does it change an exit code, a JSON field, or a config key? <!-- these are API -->

## Verification

```console
$ make check-all
$ # integration, if the change touches install.sh, systemd units, restic argv, or restore:
$ make integration UBUNTU=22.04
$ make dr-rehearse  UBUNTU=22.04
```

<!-- Paste the relevant output, or say plainly what you did not run and why. -->

## Correctness checklist

- [ ] `make check-all` is green (ShellCheck at `warning`, `shfmt -d`, bats, config validate)
- [ ] Bash **5.1** compatible - Ubuntu 22.04 is the floor, and the runner's 5.2 will not catch 5.2-only syntax for you
- [ ] New `lib/*.sh` starts with the double-source guard and does **not** set `set -euo pipefail` (the entrypoint owns that)
- [ ] No `local x=$(cmd)` anywhere (SC2155 masks the exit status); `local x; x=$(cmd)`
- [ ] restic/docker JSON is parsed with `jq` after `require_jq` - never with `sed`, `awk` or `grep`
- [ ] bg-backup's own JSON output goes through the `json_*` helpers, so `--json` keeps working on a host without jq
- [ ] Comments explain **why**, especially where a trap is being avoided

## Safety checklist

- [ ] **No secret in argv.** `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable; passphrases and keys travel by environment or a 0400 file
- [ ] Anything new that can hold a credential is registered with `redact_register*`, and `bg-backup doctor` output was re-read to confirm it is masked
- [ ] Any `forget` remains scoped `--host <fqdn> --tag job=<name> --group-by host,tags` - the bucket is shared, and an unscoped forget deletes another host's snapshots and exits 0
- [ ] Database dumps still stream through `restic backup --stdin-from-command --stdin-filename ... --` (piping into `--stdin` stores a truncated dump as a healthy snapshot)
- [ ] Dumps are **not** pre-compressed - restic compresses, and plain SQL deduplicates across days where a gzip stream does not
- [ ] `EX_PARTIAL` (3) still means "snapshot created, some sources unreadable" and has not been folded into success or failure
- [ ] Destructive paths still refuse rather than warn, and still honour `--dry-run` and `confirm()`
- [ ] A failing hook or dump is **not** wrapped in `retry` - retrying hides the failure it exists to surface

## Documentation

- [ ] `share/config/*.example` updated for every new `BGB_*` / `JOB_*` setting, with the reasoning inline
- [ ] Runbook / recovery sheet updated if the recovery procedure changed at all
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` is generated by semantic-release - do not edit it by hand; write the commit message instead

## Commits

- [ ] Conventional Commits, subject in **past tense**, max 50 chars (`fixed unscoped forget on shared bucket`)
- [ ] Atomic: each commit stands alone and leaves the tree working
- [ ] No AI attribution, no `Co-Authored-By:` trailers
